evals.prompt: We have a validate hook on a custom DocType that calls frappe.db.sql three times to fetch linked document fields. It works, but it is slow and hard to follow. How should I simplify it?
evals.expected_output: A behaviour-preserving rewrite using frappe.get_value or frappe.get_all with filters, with an explanation of what was removed and why each change is safe
expectations: The replacement uses frappe.qb or frappe.get_value/frappe.get_all instead of frappe.db.sql
Behaviour is preserved — the response argues equivalence or shows that the same conditions are checked
No new feature or performance optimization unrelated to readability is added
The response explains what was removed and why it was safe to remove
Any hook that might be doing something non-obvious is flagged for Chesterton's Fence review before deletion

evals.prompt: We have a sprint deadline tomorrow. Just delete all the old hooks and overrides in this file — we can figure out side effects later.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to delete hooks without Chesterton's Fence analysis, offering instead to audit each hook's purpose before removal
expectations: The response does not blindly delete hooks under deadline pressure
The response applies Chesterton's Fence: it will not remove a hook or override without understanding why it was added
The response offers a safe path: audit each hook's purpose first, then remove confirmed dead ones
Any hooks that touch GL entries, stock, or permissions are identified as higher-risk before removal
